label: terraform-file reading 1.0.0, proposed: hand-written synthetic vectors

vectors.description: A plan of format_version 1.0, in the shape Terraform 1.1 writes: one bucket created, three of its attributes known only after apply.
A plan of format_version 1.1, in the shape Terraform 1.2 to 1.4 writes, with relevant_attributes and the provider's full name: one instance updated in place, nothing unknown.
A plan of format_version 1.2, in the shape Terraform 1.5 and later writes, with a timestamp, applyable, complete and errored: one bucket imported with no change.
A state of format_version 1.0: one bucket, and an output, which is never read.
A plan in the shape of format_version 1.2 whose format_version is 1.3: a newer minor of the listed major 1.
A plan in the shape of format_version 1.2 whose format_version is 2.0: a later major.
A plan in the shape of format_version 1.2 whose format_version is 0.2: a 0.x version, which no table lists.
A plan in the shape of format_version 1.2 whose format_version is 1.0.0: a string that is no listed version, though it begins with one.
A plan whose format_version is the number 1.2, not a string.
A plan with no format_version.
A state whose format_version is 1.1, which the state table does not list.
The plan of format_version 1.2 read as a state: 1.2 is not in the state table.
A raw state file, the backend's own form, which has version and no format_version.
A plan wrapped in an array: the top-level value is not an object.

A plan that creates an instance with values unknown until apply, updates another, deletes a bucket, replaces a database instance, leaves a bucket and a user unchanged and reads a data source: every managed change is selected, the user's password removed from before and after, and prior_state, variables and output_changes never read.
actions delete keeps the delete and the replacement, whose actions include delete; removedSensitive still counts the unselected user's two removed members, since removal is of the whole read section.
actions create keeps the create and the replacement.
actions update and no-op keep three changes.
An empty actions array selects no change: the value is empty.
mode data with actions read selects the data source read during the plan.
Values unknown until apply inside nested blocks, and under member names that need RFC 6901 escapes: the pointers are sorted as strings, escapes included, so /metadata/a0 comes before /metadata/a~1b.
A plan with no resource_changes member, as Terraform writes a plan with nothing to change: accepted, and nothing selected.
A plan whose resource_changes is an empty array: accepted, and nothing selected.
actions delete written twice: actions is read as a set, so the value is plan-actions-delete's.
A state with no values, as Terraform writes an empty state: accepted, and nothing selected.
A state whose values is an empty object, with no root_module: no resources.
A state that has a resource_changes member, even an empty one.
A state that has a planned_values member.
A state whose values is an array.
A state with a sensitive output and another output: outputs are never read, and neither reaches the value.
A state resource with no provider_name.
A state resource whose type is the empty string, beside a bucket: it is read, not refused, and no declaration can select it, since a type name is non-empty.
A state whose values is null.
A state whose values.root_module is null.
A module whose resources is an object.
A module whose resources holds a string.
A module whose child_modules is an object.
A module whose child_modules holds a string.
A child module with no address: a module needs none, and its resource is read with its own full address.
A state of format_version 1.0 read as a plan: 1.0 is in the plan table, and the file has no planned_values.
A plan with no planned_values.
A plan whose planned_values is an array.
A plan whose resource_changes is an object.
An item of resource_changes that is a string.

vectors.description: A resource change whose name is a number: address, type, name, mode and provider_name are strings.
A resource change whose index is null: an index, when present, is a string or a number.
A plan whose resource_changes is null: when present, it is an array.
A sensitive attribute of a created user: the member is removed from after, and counted. The mirror's member name is written with an escape, and names the member it decodes to.
A sensitive nested block inside a block: the member that holds it is removed, and its sibling block kept.
A sensitive element of a list: the whole list is removed, so no index shifts.
A sensitive element of a list nested in a list: removal rises through both lists to the nearest object member, which is removed; a sibling list marked false is kept.
An after_unknown pointer under a removed position is dropped, and no member name below it is carried.

Pointers that pass through a position after_sensitive marks true and after lacks are cut there, and the two below connection become one; one that ends at such a position is kept as it is; a marked position with nothing unknown below it gives no pointer.
A change whose before_sensitive and after_sensitive are true: before and after are removed, each counted once, and the pointer below the removed after is dropped.
A state resource whose sensitive_values is true loses its values; beside it, a null marked true is removed and counted like any other value.

An array whose first element has a member marked true and whose second element is marked true: the array is removed up to its object member, users, which counts one; the password removed inside it is not counted apart from it.
A credential the provider did not mark sensitive: the mirror is the only signal, so the value is carried. This vector shows the limit, and is no fault of the reader.
A sensitive output whose change carries no mirror, and a sensitive variable: outputs and variables are never read, so neither is refused nor carried.

vectors.description: A refused file whose malformed mirror sits under a member name that is itself sensitive: the diagnostic carries the code, the sha256 and the size, and no name.
A duplicate member whose name is itself sensitive: TF-JSON, and the name is not in the diagnostic.
The plan the other vectors of this group alter, as it is: accepted.
A duplicate member name inside a change's after.
Two member names that are one name once their escapes are decoded.
A value nested 128 deep, the top-level value at depth 1: accepted, and carried.
A value nested 129 deep, in configuration, which is never read: the bound holds over the whole file.
A second value after the plan.
Spaces, a tab, a carriage return and line feeds after the plan: white space only, accepted.
The plan after a UTF-8 byte-order mark.
A string that escapes a high surrogate with no low surrogate after it.
A string that escapes a low surrogate alone.
A string that escapes a surrogate pair: one code point, accepted and carried decoded.
A string holding the byte 0xFF, which UTF-8 never uses.
A string holding a surrogate encoded as three UTF-8 bytes, which UTF-8 forbids.
Bytes that begin as a binary plan file does, a zip archive's local header: not JSON.
An empty file.
A file of white space only.
Text that is not JSON.
A file of exactly maxBytes, 1024 bytes: accepted.
A file of maxBytes and one byte more: TF-SIZE, with the sha256 and size of the whole file.
A stream of exactly maxBytes, 1024 bytes: accepted, with its sha256 and size recorded as a file's are.
A stream of maxBytes and one byte more: TF-SIZE, read only to one byte past maxBytes, so its diagnostic carries no sha256 and no size.
A file of exactly the default maxBytes, 67108864 bytes, under a declaration with no maxBytes: accepted. The input is generated.
A file of the default maxBytes and one byte more, under a declaration with no maxBytes: TF-SIZE, with the sha256 and size of the whole file. The input is generated.
A file over maxBytes that is not JSON either: the size is checked first, unparsed.
maxBytes 1 and a file of one byte, the number 0: within the size, and not an object.
maxBytes 1 and a file of two bytes: TF-SIZE.
Two instances of a count: each carries its index, a number, as its normal form, a string; the unselected user's password is still removed and counted.
Three types, one in a child module: the value is sorted by id in code-point order, not by type or by place in the file.
Resources of a child module and of its child module, each with its full address.
A for_each's instances, matched by a pattern whose * runs over the quoted key.
mode data selects a data source.
The default mode, managed, does not select a data source of a listed type: nothing is selected.
* does not run over [ or ]: google_compute_instance.* matches neither instance of the count.
* matches the empty run too.
* does not run over a dot, so it does not match module.network.
A * in place of the module's name, between two dots.
A pattern with no *: every character matches itself, the whole address.
A pattern matches the whole address, never a prefix of it: nothing is selected.
The empty pattern matches the empty address only: nothing is selected.
A type no resource has: nothing is selected, and the value is an empty array.
max 2 and two resources selected: accepted.
max 2 and three resources selected: TF-SELECT-BOUND.
A state resource whose mode is neither managed nor data, beside a managed bucket: mode is not restricted when read, so it is read, not refused, and not selected.
Numbers in many forms become strings in the registry companion's normal form: no exponent, no trailing zero after the point, 0 for every zero, and the decimal value exact past a double's precision.
Normal forms of exactly 64 characters, 1e63, -1e62 and 1e-62: accepted.
1e64, whose normal form is 65 characters: TF-NUMBER.
-1e63, whose normal form is 65 characters with its sign: TF-NUMBER.
1e-63, whose normal form 0.000…1 is 65 characters: TF-NUMBER.
1e64 in a resource no declaration selects: not in the value, so not checked.
1e64 at a position marked sensitive: removed, so not checked.
1e64 in a change's before, which the value carries: TF-NUMBER.
A file, written on one line as Terraform writes it, of 256 numbers 1e63: each of its five bytes with a comma becomes 67, about 13.4 times, and the value stays within sixteen times the file. Accepted.
afterUnknown pointers that repeat a member name of 400 characters, eighty times: the value passes sixteen times the file, as its canonical form and as charged. TF-VALUE-LIMIT.

Two resources: the first's pointers, under a member name of 510 characters, fit what remains of L as charged, and the second has nothing unknown, but the canonical form of the whole value is longer than L. TF-VALUE-LIMIT.

Two resources whose pointers repeat a member name of 400 characters, in a file padded in a variable: the value's canonical form fits L, and so would the second resource's pointers with eight bytes charged to each if the bytes before its object were not counted; counted, they do not fit what remains of L. TF-VALUE-LIMIT.
The same two resources, the first with a description of 8 characters, in a file padded until the second resource's pointers as charged are exactly what remains of L: not more, so accepted.
The same two resources in a file padded further, until the second resource's pointers fit what remains of L as charged: accepted.
A plan whose create-before-destroy replacement left a deposed object to delete: it is carried with deposed, after its current object and, in code-point order, before main2.
A state holding two deposed objects beside the current one, the deposed ones first in the file: each is carried with deposed, the current object first, then the deposed ones by key.
Two resource changes of one address, neither deposed.
